prompt: Write a note to a friend about a quarrel and making up afterward. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the note only.
final_message:
Hey Sam,

I've been meaning to write this since Sunday, because I don't think a text would do it justice.

First, I'm sorry. I said things at dinner that I didn't mean, and a few that I did mean but should have said differently, or at a better time. When you mentioned you couldn't make the trip, I heard "I don't care about this" instead of what you were actually telling me: that you were stretched thin and felt guilty about it. I made it about me, and then I got sharp with you in front of everyone. That wasn't fair.

I've been replaying the argument all week. Somewhere around Wednesday I realized I wasn't really angry about the trip. I was scared that we were drifting, that the friendship was slipping into the kind where we only see each other when it's convenient. Instead of saying that, I picked a fight about logistics. Classic me.

I also want you to know that I'm not asking you to apologize back. You had your own side of it, and I'd like to hear it properly, whenever you're ready. I think we both said some things on autopilot. But I'd rather figure out the real stuff together than keep circling the same argument.

Here's what I'd love: let me take you to that terrible diner we used to go to after class. Pancakes on me, no agenda, no scorekeeping. If we want to talk about the trip, we can. If we'd rather argue about whether their coffee is actually good, that works too. (It isn't. You know it isn't.)

You've been one of my people for a long time, and a bad night doesn't change that. If anything, it reminded me how much I'd hate to lose you over something so avoidable.

No pressure to answer right away. Take whatever time you need. But the offer stands, and so do I.

Saturday morning, if you're free? Or any day that works.

Your friend,
Alex
